hook_text: If South Africa's water were a pie, who would get the biggest slice? It's not your household.
clip_script: Picture all of South Africa's water as one big pie. The biggest slice, about sixty percent, goes to farmers irrigating fruit, vegetables, sugar cane and wheat. That's more than half the pie. The next slice, about twenty-seven percent, goes to towns and cities: homes, schools, hospitals and businesses. The thin slices left over go to forestry plantations, factories, mines, power stations and livestock. The law says water belongs to everyone, and people's basic needs and healthy rivers come first. Fixing leaks is the cheapest way to make the pie go further.
visual_style: An animated pie chart is drawn slice by slice with a protractor; icons appear on each slice: a tractor, a house, a factory, a mine, a pine tree, a cow; a dripping tap gets fixed.
pacing: One slice at a time, ending with a punchy tip.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson on who uses South Africa's water.
